results.question: How much is the monthly fee on the everyday account and how do I avoid paying it?
results.answer:
The Everyday Account has a monthly fee of KES 250. You can avoid it in either of two ways:

- **Salary paid in:** The KES 250 monthly fee is waived for any month in which your salary is paid into your Kaskazi Everyday Account. The salary must come from your employer. Money you move yourself from another account, money paid in as cash, money sent from a mobile money wallet, and payments from friends, family or customers do not count as salary.
- **Average balance of KES 50,000 or more:** The bank adds up the balance in your account at the end of each day of the month, then divides by the number of days in the month. A balance that dips below KES 50,000 on some days can still qualify, as long as the monthly average is KES 50,000 or more.

You only need one waiver to apply. If you're self-employed or paid in cash, you won't qualify for the salary waiver, but you can still use the average balance waiver.

You can open it in the app in about 10 minutes by photographing your student ID with your other documents. There is no minimum opening balance, and the account has no monthly fee. results.question: why cant i withdraw more than 20k a day from my student acount??
results.answer:
The KES 20,000 limit is there to protect students' money. To keep your money safer while you study, the Kaskazi Student Account has a daily withdrawal limit of KES 20,000. Students often carry cash on campus and share accommodation. If your card and PIN are stolen, the most a thief can take in cash in a day is KES 20,000.

The limit covers all cash withdrawals added together, at Kaskazi ATMs, other banks' ATMs, agents and branches. The KES 20,000 daily limit can't be raised on a Kaskazi Student Account.

For large payments such as rent or fees, pay by transfer or card instead of cash. School fees payments from your Kaskazi account are free. When a Kaskazi Student Account converts to a Kaskazi Everyday Account, the standard Kaskazi Debit Card ATM limit of KES 100,000 a day applies from then on.

results.question: what does 'up to 50 days interest free' actually mean? do I get 50 days on everything I buy with the credit card?
results.answer:
No, not everything gets 50 days. "Up to 50 days" is the longest period, and the number you get depends on when in the statement period you buy. The interest-free period runs from the day you make a purchase to the payment due date of the statement that purchase appears on. A purchase made on the first day of a statement period waits the longest before it is due, so it gets the full 50 days. A purchase made on the last day of a statement period gets the fewest days.

In the bank's example, a statement period runs from 1 May to 31 May, with a payment due date of 20 June. A purchase on 1 May gets 50 days, one on 15 May gets 36 days, and one on 31 May gets 20 days.

You only keep the interest-free period when you pay your full statement balance by the payment due date. It does not apply to cash advances. If you pay less, interest of 2.5% a month is charged on the balance you carry over.

results.question: Can I approve a personal loan where total repayments come to 42% of net pay if the customer's credit record is clean?
results.answer:
No, the 40% limit has no exceptions. We do not make exceptions to the 40% limit, because it is there to protect you. A repayment total of 42% of net pay is over the limit, so the loan can't go ahead as it stands. A clean credit record doesn't change that. To bring the repayments within 40%, the applicant could borrow less, choose a longer term, or wait until an existing loan is smaller or repaid. If the loan is being used to clear another loan in full, the bank can leave that repayment out of the calculation, but only as long as the loan is cleared from the new money and you show us proof that it has been closed.

results.question: how is the personal loan interest worked out, is it linked to the base rate?
results.answer:
Yes. The Kaskazi Personal Loan rate is linked to the Kaskazi Base Rate. It is made of two parts: the Kaskazi Base Rate, which is currently 11.5% a year and is set by Kaskazi Bank, and a margin of 4.0 percentage points, which stays the same for the whole life of your loan. That gives the 15.5% a year.

Interest is worked out monthly on what you still owe. Each month, interest is the monthly rate (15.5% divided by 12) applied to the balance you owe at the start of that month. Your instalment pays that month's interest first, and the rest reduces the balance.

If the Base Rate changes, your rate moves by the same amount. When the rate changes, we recalculate your instalment on the balance you then owe, over the months left in your term, so your loan still ends on the same date. We write to you in the app before the change takes effect, telling you the new rate, your new instalment and the date it starts.

For a worked example, on a KES 500,000 loan over 36 months, the first month's interest is about KES 6,458.33, because you owe the full KES 500,000. The arrangement fee and insurance are separate from interest. Both are deducted from the loan before the money is paid to you.
